subject: Order Schedule: questions on tier conciliation, caps/floors, and packaging
messages:
From: Ava Simmons <ava.simmons@novushealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@novushealth.com
Date: 2028-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on order schedule — caps/floors and packaging

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. The procurement team reviewed the order schedule and we have a few items that need clarification before we can route this to legal and finance: 

- Exhibit pricing table: the "stability floor" language isn't clear about whether it applies per model or at the account aggregate. Can you confirm intent?
- Tiering bands: we saw a note about "packaged bundles" with a different per-token rate for embedding-heavy workloads — is that a permanent SKU or a temporary promotional band?
- Caps/concessions: procurement asked if there is a true upper-cap on monthly spend for the initial 12 months or if the 'soft cap' is purely advisory.

We also noticed a reference to a "reconciliation true-up" with a 60-day window. Our finance team prefers 30 days for faster alignment; will that be acceptable?

We can upload a marked PDF if helpful.

Best,
Ava Simmons
Senior Procurement Manager
Novus Health

Subject: Re: Questions on order schedule — caps/floors and packaging

Hi Ava —

Thanks — this is a helpful list. I've attached a lightly annotated draft of the pricing exhibit (pricing-exhibit_v3_redlines.pdf) and a draft order schedule spreadsheet with two alternative rows for the embedding-heavy bundle. High-level responses below: 

1) Stability floor scope: our intent was per-account aggregate (sits at the account level so different models can be counted together). The reason is to avoid customers having to treat every model as a separate commitment when they shift workloads. If Novus prefers model-level floors for compliance reasons we can add a note.

2) Packaged bundle: the embedding bundle is a permanent SKU in our catalog (we introduced it last year) but the promotional pricing shown in Exhibit v2 was an introductory concession. In the attached draft I separated permanent SKU pricing vs. promotional pilot band so legal can pick which to include.

3) Upper-cap: the language we used is a soft cap with a mitigation ladder (notifications, throttling options, grace credits). We can add a hard cap option for a committed reserved capacity addendum if you need a guaranteed ceiling — that would typically convert to Dedicated capacity pricing.

4) True-up window: we can accept 30 days. I flagged the clause for Marissa to confirm legal comfort.

Next steps I propose:
- Novus marks preferred options on the PDF and returns with a redline
- We prepare a short MOU that captures whether you want (A) account-level floor, (B) model-level floors, and (C) hard-cap vs soft-cap approach

Looping in Marissa for legal wording and Ben for cost impact modeling on the embedding bundle.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Hi all —

Quick read of Naomi's annotated exhibit and a few legal redline notes attached: see pricing-exhibit_v3_redlines.pdf (I've added trackable comments). Summary of the legal concerns that need explicit language: 

- "Stability floor" definition: if we keep aggregate language we need a clear metric definition ("billable units" defined as tokens for generation + embedding units for embeddings) and a reconciliation table example. Ambiguity here creates audit risk.
- Cap mechanics: our current "soft cap" construct contains a remediation ladder; Novus asked for a hard cap — we can draft an addendum that defines "Hard Cap" as an explicit dollar limit and a late-termination remedy if exceeded without amendment. Note that a hard cap will materially affect pricing and capacity guarantees (Karthik: please add numbers to the spreadsheet scenario).
- Packaged bundles: the promotional pilot language should expire with a defined "pilot end date" and require written consent to extend. For evergreen SKUs, include an annual notice window for price adjustments (60 days minimum).
- True-up: 30-day window acceptable; change references from "calendar days" to "business days" per Novus preference.

Ava — for procurement ease, please indicate on the PDF whether Novus wants: 
  1) Account-level floor (aggregate counting) OR model-level floors;
  2) Hard cap (reserved capacity addendum) OR soft cap with mitigation ladder;
  3) Pilot extension terms for the embedding band (Y/N + target end date).

We prefer to avoid indefinite promotional pricing without approval windows. Once we have your selection we will produce an MOU + redlined order schedule for final sign-off.

Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Questions on order schedule — caps/floors and packaging

Marissa, Naomi — thanks for the quick turnaround and the annotated draft. Novus' initial positions below (we'll provide a marked PDF by Friday):

1) Floors: prefer account-level aggregate counting to avoid operational complexity across model swaps. We request an example reconciliation table in the MOU.
2) Cap: will proceed with a soft cap + mitigation ladder for the pilot year. We may convert to a hard cap if monthly usage exceeds forecasted thresholds during Q3/Q4.
3) Embedding bundle: accept permanent SKU pricing but request a 90-day pilot pricing window to evaluate actual unit economics. We agree to the 30-business-day true-up.

One open ask: can Redwood include a one-time credit (up to $15k) if Novus converts to Dedicated capacity within the first 12 months? That will help us justify the pilot to finance.

We'll return the marked PDF with the selections and any small language tweaks. Appreciate the responsiveness — will loop legal next.

Best,
Ava Simmons
Senior Procurement Manager
Novus Health
